title: Research notes: Prestonsburg
summary: Sources for Preston’s Station (1797), Floyd County (1799–1800), the 1808 courthouse fire, and the 1818 establishment. The brief’s John Graham and May 3, 1797 details were not confirmed.

items.text: Area part of the 100,000-acre grant to the family of Elizabeth Patton Preston, administered by John Preston.
John Spurlock of Montgomery County, Va., arrived 1791 and laid out Preston’s Station in 1797.
Renamed to honor Col. John Preston, landowner.
Contested: the brief credited surveyor John Graham and a May 3, 1797 plat; its source was an AI encyclopedia and was not used.
Floyd County created Dec. 13, 1799, effective June 1, 1800, from Fleming, Montgomery and Mason; named for John Floyd; seat at Preston’s Station.
First courthouse burned April 8, 1808, destroying early records.
Post office ‘Floyd Court House’ 1816 to late 1820s; town formally established 1818.
Brief’s ‘six residents in the 1800 census’ was cut: not found in the sources.

timeline.event: Floyd County takes effect; Preston’s Station is the seat.

openQuestions: Primary record of the 1797 plat and who drew it (Spurlock vs. Graham).
Exact date of the 1818 act establishing the town.

sources.citation: “Prestonsburg.” Kentucky Secretary of State, Land Office city record.
